# std.kv

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Key/value helpers: the shape every configuration block, header read and
form parser uses.

A `Map<K, V>` is the natural shape for lookup, but parsing produces a
list of pairs, and a few places (environment variables, form fields)
want the list form. `from_list` and `to_list` convert between the two;
the rest are the map operations under the name a parser site expects.

## Functions

### `filter`

```badger
fn filter<K, V>(m: Map<K, V>, keep: fn(K, V) -> Bool) -> Map<K, V> where K: Hash
```

The entries `keep` accepts.

### `from_list`

```badger
fn from_list<K, V>(entries: List<(K, V)>) -> Map<K, V> where K: Hash
```

A map from a list of pairs (later duplicates win).

### `get`

```badger
fn get<K, V>(m: Map<K, V>, key: K) -> Option<V>
```

The value at `key`, if any.

### `get_or`

```badger
fn get_or<K, V>(m: Map<K, V>, key: K, default: V) -> V
```

The value at `key`, or `default`.

### `len`

```badger
fn len<K, V>(m: Map<K, V>) -> Int
```

How many entries the map has.

### `map_keys`

```badger
fn map_keys<K, V, W>(m: Map<K, V>, f: fn(K) -> W) -> Map<W, V> where W: Hash
```

The same entries with `f` applied to each key.

### `map_values`

```badger
fn map_values<K, V, W>(m: Map<K, V>, f: fn(V) -> W) -> Map<K, W> where K: Hash
```

The same entries with `f` applied to each value.

### `merge`

```badger
fn merge<K, V>(a: Map<K, V>, b: Map<K, V>) -> Map<K, V> where K: Hash
```

Both maps' entries; `b`'s win where both have a key.

### `to_list`

```badger
fn to_list<K, V>(m: Map<K, V>) -> List<(K, V)>
```

The entries of a map, in its entry order.
